Where it began

Sunil Narine was born in Arima, Trinidad, and bowls off-spin with his right arm while batting left-handed. His first-class debut for Trinidad and Tobago, in February 2009, brought no wickets from thirteen overs, and almost a year passed before his next game.

Things moved quickly after that. In 2011 Trinidad and Tobago won the Caribbean Twenty20, and at the Champions League that followed only two other bowlers reached ten wickets as he did. Later that year he was the leading wicket-taker as they won the Regional Super50, five clear of anyone else.

The player

His one-day international debut came in India in December 2011, and his first two victims were Virat Kohli and Ravichandran Ashwin as the West Indies won by 16 runs. Early in 2012 he took 31 wickets in three first-class matches at 9.61 each, and in June he made his Test debut against England after only six first-class games.

In just his second Test he took eight wickets, including his first five-wicket haul, and was named man of the match. He played 6 Tests between 2012 and 2013, taking 21 wickets at 40.52 with two five-wicket hauls and a best of 6 for 91. He was part of the West Indies side that won the 2012 World Twenty20, and he retired from international cricket in November 2023.

What made him special

Variety, and the art of hiding it. His off-breaks came in a whole family of variations, and he disguised them so well that he was known as a mystery bowler. In the Champions League T20 he took 39 wickets, and by November 2026 nobody had taken more in that competition.

His Test batting was a modest business, 40 runs at 8.00 with a best of 22 not out. T20 cricket told a different story. Against Rajasthan Royals in April 2024 he made his first IPL hundred, 109 off only 56 balls. It is a fine reason never to judge a man by his Test batting average.

Away from the middle

Franchise cricket became his home. He joined Kolkata Knight Riders in 2012 and was named the IPL's most valuable player that season, again in 2018 and a third time in 2024, when Kolkata took their third title. Nobody had won the award three times before. In 2024 he also became the fourth man to play 500 T20 matches and the first spinner to get there, and in May 2026 he took his 200th IPL wicket, the first bowler from overseas to get there. Along the way he played for Knight Riders sides in other leagues, as well as for teams in Canada, Bangladesh and England.

And finally

A maiden over is hard enough to bowl in a Test. Bowling one in a Super Over, when the batsmen have six balls and nothing to lose, was something only he had managed by November 2026. It may be the most Sunil Narine line in the record books.
